sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of respondent-State.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11207025211430/2021 registered with the Godhra 'A' Division Police Station, Panchmahal for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Learned advocate Ms. Vyas for the applicant submitted that in connection with the aforesaid FIR,
the applicant has already been granted bail by the Coordinate Bench of this Court by an order dated 10.03.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Application No. 1171 of 2022, however as per one of the conditions, the applicant has to remain present before the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5101/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined concerned trial court but she was not remained present and, hence, the concerned court was constrained to issue non- bailable Manjulaben Ambalal Pandya vs State Of Gujarat on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17211955/

sentences.text: 1 warrant against the present applicant, which was eventually served and since 23.02.2024, the applicant is in judicial custody.

Learned advocate further submitted that the applicant assures to this Hon'ble Court that if the applicant is released on bail, she will abide by all the conditions, which may be imposed upon her and also will remain present before the concerned Court as and when the date is fixed, for which, the applicant is also ready and willing to file an undertaking to that effect.
It is, therefore, submitted that the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
4. Learned APP for the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

It is submitted that trial has got delayed due to non- appearance of the present applicant before the concerned court and, hence considering above facts, the present application may not be entertained.
5. Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

6. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.

It is found out that the applicant has already been granted bail in connection with the present FIR but as she remained absent consequently on 3 occasions, the concerned court has issued NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5101/2024 ORDER DATED:
14/03/2024 undefined non-bailable warrant upon the applicant - accused, which was eventually served and since then, she is in judicial custody.
Further as stated above, assurance has been given by the applicant to remain present before the concerned court as and when the date is fixed.
Therefore considering above factual aspects of the matter, the present application deserves consideration with certain strict conditions.

7. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40 as well as in case of Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51.
8.
